LESSON: MAIN PHYSICAL FEATURES IN KENYA -RELIEF -DRAINAGE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 1.3: Main physical features in Kenya -Relief -Drainage
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Main physical features in Kenya -Relief -Drainage, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why are physical features useful in a country?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Main physical features in Kenya -Relief -Drainage together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: Learners engage in assigned roles as they collect and display maps and pictures showing the main physical features in Kenya.

● Respect: Learners appreciate diverse opinions as they brainstorm in groups to identify physical features found in Kenya.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learners care for the physical features found in the immediate environment.

Link to other learning areas:

● Learners will apply drawing skills as they draw a map of Kenya and locate the main physical features.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Resource persons, maps, tactile maps, digital resources with assistive technology, charts, tactile charts, marker pens, approved text books and

other printed resources or braille resources.
